steps.label: Binary Place Values
steps.content:
1.1 Number Systems

Binary Place Values

Year 11

  • Today: why computers use binary.
  • The place values of a binary number, and why they double.
  • How to turn a binary number into denary.
Think → Pair → ShareWhy do you think a computer needs its own number system?Show the answer

A computer is built from switches that are on or off. It needs numbers made from just two digits.

steps.label: Why Computers Use Binary
steps.content:
Why Computers Use Binary

Think → Pair → SharePredict: a switch can only be on or off. Why does a computer need only two digits?Show the worked answer

A switch has two states. One digit for each state is enough: 0 for off, 1 for on.

So a computer stores everything as 0s and 1s.

  • A computer has billions of tiny switches.
  • Each switch is on or off. There are only two states.
  • Off is 0. On is 1.
  • A number made of only 0s and 1s is binary.
  • One binary digit is a bit.
  • Binary is base 2: 2 digits. Denary is base 10: 10 digits.

steps.label: Why Each Place Value Doubles
steps.content:
Why Each Place Value Doubles

Think → Pair → ShareCount in binary: 0, then 1. A column can only hold 0 or 1. Predict: why does 2 need a new column?Show the worked answer

At 1 the first column is full. There is no digit 2, so we write 10: a 1 in a new column.

That new column is worth 2. The next new column starts at 4, then 8: each one double the last.

  • Each column holds only 0 or 1.
  • When a column is full, we start a new column on the left. Denary does this too: 9, then 10.
  • In binary a new column starts at 1, 2, 4, 8.
  • So each place value is double the one on its right.

The 8 Place Values

Think → Pair → ShareThe place values start 1, 2, 4, 8 from the right. Predict the next four. Why?Show the worked answer

16, 32, 64, 128. Each one is double the one before it.

  • Start with 1 on the right.
  • Double each time as you move left.
  • A binary number with 8 bits is an 8-bit number. It has 8 place values.
128←64←32←16←8←4←2←1

Moving left: times 2 each time.

A 0 means off. That column adds nothing.

We only add the place values with a 1 under them.

  • A 4-bit number has 4 place values: 8, 4, 2, 1.
  • Write the place values above the bits.
  • A 1: add that place value.
  • A 0: add nothing.
  • The total is the denary value.

steps.label: Why 11111111 Is 255
steps.content:
Why 11111111 Is 255

Think → Pair → ShareEvery bit is 1: 11111111. Predict its denary value. Why can no 8-bit number be bigger?Show the worked answer

128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255.

Every place value is already added. One more would need a 9th column, worth 256.

  • Largest: every bit is 1, so every place value is added.
  • 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255.
  • Smallest: every bit is 0. 00000000 is 0.
  • One more than 255 needs a 9th column, worth 256. An 8-bit number has no 9th column.

Largest: 255
